pending: **The bug:** `"Battery Hold Down Bolt for 2006-2012 Ford Escape, Focus, Mercury Mariner Models"` is a genuine wrong-merge (it claims a 2006 Escape fits; it does not). Because the word "Models" appears *anywhere*, it downgrades to `"warn"`. `part-panel.tsx` then renders the Alert: *"The amber flags are a judgment call, not a defect… Red is what needs fixing."* **We caption a real defect as benign.** This is the exact complaint JEGS rejected the batch over.

**Fix:** a legitimate collapse looks like `for <range> <Make> <FamilyTerm>` with **no enumerated model list**. Only downgrade when the name does NOT enumerate multiple vehicles — i.e. the family term is adjacent to the offending range and there is no comma-separated model list between them. Do not just widen the regex; scope it to the text around the offending range.

**Test fix (mandatory):** `frontend/src/app/lab/jegs-fitment/jegs-fitment.checks.test.ts`. The existing test asserts only `expect(v).toHaveLength(1)` — **presence, never severity** — so it passes whether the row is an error or a warning. **Assert `severity`.** Then mutation-test: revert the fix, confirm the test goes RED, restore.

**The bug:** a partial fitment deliberately sets `fitment_notes`, NOT `content_error`, so `unverified` is `False`. `_derive_fits_select` therefore skips its `return ""` guard and computes Y/N from the **surviving** years only. If the dropped (contested) vehicle was the one reaching the current model year, Fits Select flips Y→N: an affirmative "does not fit" derived from data withheld **for being unreliable**. `_derive_fits_select`'s own docstring forbids exactly this.

**Fix:** keep `unverified = bool(content_error)` for `fitment_kind` (that is correct), but Fits Select must also be blank on a partial. Pass a separate flag, e.g. `_derive_fits_select(..., unknown=bool(content_error) or bool(fitment_notes))`.
**Test:** construct a partial where the **contested** vehicle carries the newest years; assert `fits_select == ""`. Mutation-test it.

**The issue:** `_execute_cached` is `@cache(Backends.EnhancementBackend, ttl=4 weeks)`; `_make_cache_key` stringifies `Args`, and pydantic's `str(Args)` includes **all fields with their defaults**. Adding the field changes every previously-cached key **for every template and every customer**, so every job re-runs the LLM for content it already had.
**ASK THE USER:** eat the one-time cache flush, or exclude defaulted fields from the cache key? Do not decide this silently.
Signature still says `-> tuple[list[dict], str]` while it returns a 3-tuple; the docstring still says "Returns (fitments, content_error)".

This is the **same class** as the crash that killed 4 SKUs live, and `backend/pyproject.toml` configures **ruff only — no mypy, no pyright** — so the annotation was the one artifact that could have caught it.

**`mustStateVehicle` fails BOTH ways** (`jegs-fitment.data.ts`, `vehicleWords` filters `w.length >= 4`): (a) any make/model under 4 chars — **Kia, GMC, BMW, RAM, Rio, Fit** — yields an empty word list, and the guard waves the row through, so a Meta_Title naming **no vehicle at all** passes. That is the customer's #1 complaint check, vacuous. (b) `"Mazda CX-5"` yields only `["Mazda"]`, so a title abbreviated to `"…for CX-5"` hard-errors — even though `MetaTitleFitment` explicitly tells the model to abbreviate.
